B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The official MCP documentation gives no separate MCP price. It requires a PagerDuty account with Advanced Permissions; the pricing page does not establish whether MCP access is available on every plan.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: The vendor pricing page lists Incident Management Free (up to 5 users) and Professional at $21 per user/month billed annually or $25 monthly. PD Reliability Platform tiers are listed from $2,800/year; other tiers and custom pricing are shown on the page.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: The pricing page describes platform subscriptions with included Seats, Events, and AI Actions, with additional capacity available through credits. No MCP per-call fee or MCP-specific quota was found.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Valid PagerDuty account with Advanced Permissions; user API key or OAuth client/token; remote MCP client required. Docs say some filters require user-level authentication. Tool filtering is not directly available; scoped OAuth can limit which tools succeed. EU accounts should use the EU endpoint.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: PagerDuty controls service availability and authorization; organization administrators control account permissions and OAuth client scopes; users control which credentials they provide.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Official hosted docs divide operations into browse and manage categories but do not publish tool annotations. The archived local variant labels read tools readOnlyHint=true and write tools destructiveHint=true; those annotations are not attributed to the hosted service. 2. No server-enforced confirmation parameter or preview/confirm flow was found in hosted docs. Product approval workflows are available as PagerDuty operations, but their enforcement in this MCP server is not documented. 3. Authentication is API key or OAuth; docs support user-level and account-level credentials and state some filters require user-level auth. OAuth metadata advertises many resource scopes, PKCE S256, token grants, and revocation. Token lifetime, redirect-URI approval rules, and allowlists are Unknown. 4. Hosted docs say tool filtering is not directly available; scoped OAuth can limit which tools succeed. US and EU endpoints are documented. No read-only hosted mode or sandbox endpoint was found. 5. Hosted MCP-specific masking, PII exclusions, and secret-field handling: Unknown. Product permissions apply to authenticated requests, but exact field boundaries are not documented. 6. API reference documents HTTP 429 and rate limiting but no MCP-specific quota. A third-party catalog reports REST API limits, which are not treated as verified MCP limits. No MCP result cap or truncation documentation found. 7. Hosted parameter validation/correction and operator overrides: Unknown; hosted schemas are not published in the checked sources. 8. Vendor logging, MCP audit attribution, and telemetry behavior/opt-out: Unknown. Pricing page includes audit trail reporting as a product capability. 9. No vendor feedback, rating, report, survey, or upsell tool was found in the listed tool names. 10. Hosted initialize instructions and server-delivered skills are not published. User-level guidance includes: “Tool filtering is not directly available for the PagerDuty-hosted server at this point in time. You can, however, limit which tools succeed by using a Scoped OAuth client.” The archived local code advises caution on writes and confirmation for destructive tools; this does not establish hosted behavior. 11. Whether past agent behavior changes future results or available context: Unknown. 12. One documented hosted endpoint per region (US/global and EU); no sub-server hierarchy documented. 13. No raw API, arbitrary SQL, script, or general request tool identified in the 63 names visible in the Claude connector directory listing; its page states 64 total, so one name was not available to inspect.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: Tool filtering is not directly available for the PagerDuty-hosted server at this point in time. You can, however, limit which tools succeed by using a Scoped OAuth client.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official hosted tool reference is https://docs.pagerduty.com/ai-automation/advance/pagerduty-mcp-server. It names 18 browse/manage groups and enumerates operations within each, but does not publish a complete machine-name list or schemas. The MCP API reference gives a list_incidents example. The Claude connector directory lists 63 exact machine names visible in its page and states “Show all 64 tools”; one name was not available to inspect. actions.json contains those 63 names. Names confirmed verbatim by official sources are marked Official; the remaining names are appended as Third-party (Claude connector directory, 2026-10). The directory describes the connector as made by PagerDuty but is classified as third-party under the required source rules. No MCP-specific tool list or total was stated by PagerDuty.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Official client guidance says some list_incidents filters require user-level authentication and that scoped OAuth can restrict which tools succeed. No server-enforced confirmation guidance was found for the hosted endpoint.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The hosted MCP docs describe OAuth/API-key authentication and a PagerDuty-hosted managed service. They do not state MCP-specific retention, training use, or logging practices. The privacy policy and terms apply broadly to PagerDuty services; they do not specify hosted MCP data handling in the checked passages.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: PagerDuty describes the hosted server as maintained by PagerDuty, remotely accessible, and requiring no local installation. The documentation says it supports OAuth and API keys.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Authentication and endpoint behavior are corroborated by supplied OAuth metadata and the endpoint’s 401 response. Tool filtering guidance describes authorization-based failures rather than a server-side tool-list filter. Other MCP-specific governance claims could not be compared with server implementation because hosted code and initialize output are unavailable.

contradictions: PagerDuty’s hosted tool reference enumerates 18 browse/manage groups and operations but does not state a total. The Claude connector directory says “Show all 64 tools”; only 63 exact machine names were visible in the collected page.

The supplied protected-resource metadata lists scopes including incidents.write and other write scopes. The hosted docs say a scoped OAuth client can limit which tools succeed, but do not describe a server-wide read-only mode.

The base protected-resource metadata URL returned HTTP 404, while the endpoint-path URL https://mcp.pagerduty.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp returned HTTP 200 and was referenced by the endpoint’s 401 challenge.

The archived public local server is deprecated and described by PagerDuty as a different local variant. Its instructions, tool annotations, and tool inventory are not evidence for the hosted endpoint.
observations_for_research: Authorization scope lists include both broad read/write scopes and resource-specific scopes, while hosted documentation says scoped OAuth can limit which tools succeed.
PagerDuty documents regional endpoint selection and authorization-based restriction of tool success; it says direct hosted tool filtering is unavailable.
